light.label: Bright indirect light
light.note: Tolerates medium light, but the white fades

landscape_use.note: Frost-free zones only; keep out of direct sun

home_use.note: Trails neatly from a shelf near a bright window

snap: A compact, trailing pothos with small heart-shaped leaves in bold patches of creamy white and green. It stays neater than most pothos and is easy to keep. It needs bright, filtered light to hold its pattern. Toxic to cats and dogs if chewed.

deep_dive.title: Origin & Habit
deep_dive.body: The pothos is native to the Society Islands in the South Pacific and now grows wild across the tropics, where it climbs tree trunks with aerial roots. The N'Joy was found as a natural branch mutation, or sport, of the Marble Queen. Its leaves are smaller and thinner than its parent's, and it grows more compactly. Indoors the vines trail or climb a pole or trellis.

deep_dive.title: Key Care Rule
deep_dive.body: Give it bright indirect light to keep the white patches. In dim light it turns greener, and direct sun scorches the white. Water when the top 3–5 cm of soil is dry, and never leave the pot standing in water. It droops when thirsty and perks up soon after a drink. Yellow, mushy leaves mean too much water.

deep_dive.title: Special Feature
deep_dive.body: The patches of white and green are larger and bolder than on the Marble Queen, on smaller, more compact leaves. That makes it a neat choice for desks, shelves and small spaces. If a shoot comes back all green, cut it back to a variegated node so the pattern doesn't take over. Trim the tips to keep it full.
